tip.title: Read between the lines
tip.text: Writers do not spell out everything. An INFERENCE is a smart conclusion from clues in the text plus what you already know. Formula: text clue + what I know = inference. If a character keeps checking his phone and tapping his foot, you can infer he is nervous, even if the word is never used. Always point to the clue that supports your inference.

passage.title: The Empty Seat
passage.text:
Dindo used to be the loudest person in Grade 9 Mabini. Then, in October, he started missing school. First one day a week. Then two. When he did come, he slept at his desk with his head on his arms.

His classmate Bea noticed other things. His shoes were the same ones from June, now with a hole near the toe. His hands had small cuts and were rough. Once, in the canteen, he counted coins twice before buying a single piece of bread.

Bea did not ask him anything in front of the others. On Friday she waited by the gate. "My tita's eatery needs someone to pass out flyers on Saturdays," she said. "Two hundred pesos and lunch. I told her I know someone." This was not exactly true. She had asked her tita for the job that morning.

Dindo looked at her for a long moment. "Okay," he said. The next week, he was in school four days. The week after, five.

words.meaning: saw or became aware of something
words.example: I noticed a crack in the screen.
The eatery near school sells cheap rice meals.
They handed out flyers for the sale.

items.prompt: Why was Dindo probably missing school and sleeping in class?
choices: He was working to earn money for his family.
He was playing games all night.
items.why: Clues: rough hands with cuts, old shoes, counting coins carefully. Together they point to work and money problems.

items.prompt: Why did Bea say "I told her I know someone" even though it was not exactly true?
choices: She wanted Dindo to accept the job without feeling like charity.
Her tita told her to say it.
items.why: She created the job for him but made it sound like a normal opening, so he could say yes with his pride intact.

items.prompt: What most likely caused the small cuts and rough skin on Dindo's hands?
choices: Sleeping with his head on his arms.
items.why: Cuts and rough hands come from hard physical work. The text pairs this clue with his missing school and counting coins, so he was working, not playing.

items.prompt: What made Bea ask her tita for the Saturday job that morning?
choices: Her tita was short of workers.
She wanted the two hundred pesos for herself.
She had noticed Dindo's problems and wanted to help him.
Dindo asked her to find him a job.
items.why: Paragraph 2 lists everything Bea noticed. Paragraph 3 says she "had asked her tita for the job that morning" and then offered it to Dindo, so his problems were the cause.

items.prompt: Why did Dindo look at Bea "for a long moment" before saying okay?
choices: He did not understand what flyers were.
He was deciding whether to accept help from a classmate.
He was angry that she waited by the gate.
He wanted more than two hundred pesos.
items.why: He had hidden his problems from everyone. The long pause shows he was weighing whether to let Bea help, and then he chose to say yes.

items.prompt: Why did Bea not ask Dindo anything in front of the others?
choices: She did not want to embarrass him.
items.why: She chose a private moment at the gate, showing she wanted to protect him from shame.

items.prompt: Which word means almost the same as "loudest" in "the loudest person in Grade 9 Mabini" (paragraph 1)?
items.why: Swap it in: "the noisiest person in Grade 9 Mabini" keeps the meaning. "Quietest" is the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word is the OPPOSITE of "rough" in "His hands had small cuts and were rough" (paragraph 2)?
items.why: Rough skin is the opposite of smooth skin. "Hard," "dirty" and "cold" describe other things, not the opposite of rough.

items.prompt: In paragraph 3, which one word means almost the same as "restaurant"? Write the word.
items.why: "My tita's eatery needs someone to pass out flyers." An eatery is a small restaurant.

items.prompt: What happened BECAUSE Dindo took the Saturday job?
choices: He slept at his desk even more.
He moved to his tita's eatery.
He started coming to school four days a week, then five.
items.why: "The next week, he was in school four days. The week after, five." The weekend money let him come back to class.
